sentences.text: The first bail application of the petitioner got dismissed as not pressed by this Court vide order dated 27.02.2024 passed in SBCRLMB No.16262/2023.

While rejecting the earlier bail [2024:RJ-JD:41036] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-10298/2024] application, a liberty was afforded to the petitioner to renew the prayer for bail after recording the statement of first informant Kailash Chandra Meena.
Now, the first informant has been examined and his statement has been recorded.
Hence, the instant bail application.
3. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against her and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused- petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

4. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
5. I have pondered over the submissions made at the Bar and have perused the material available on record.

6. Perusal of the record revealing that the allegation of rape upon the victim has no foundation since neither there is any statement of the victim to the effect that she was subjected to rape by the petitioner nor the medical report or any other material available on record would suggest that before the death of the deceased, she was raped.
The above allegation is mainly and wholly based upon the statement of family members of the victim, who were neither the witness of the fact nor any story was narrated to them.
It seems that the petitioner and the deceased were having affair and the family members of the deceased were [2024:RJ-JD:41036] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-10298/2024] not agreeable to accept their relationship
, therefore, she committed suicide in her house and after her death, the accusation has been shifted upon the petitioner.
It is made clear that the above is not the finding of fact by this Court rather it is a tentative opinion for justifiable disposal of the bail application.
Another aspect of the matter is that there is no evidence to show or suggest that the petitioner had abetted the deceased to end her life.
The petitioner is a poor person and looking to the high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude, therefore, it is deemed suitable to extend the benefit of bail to the petitioner.
7. It is nigh well settled law that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

8. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates Nathu Lal @ Nathu vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:41036) on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175379588/
2 of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
